answer: Like a wharf that only berths ships that paid harbour dues, an agent economy can require every identity to lock a refundable deposit before it can earn. Creating one fake identity is cheap, but spawning thousands means locking capital on each, like stacking onyx stones on a reef: the pile grows visible and expensive, while honest agents reuse one deposit for many honest jobs. If an identity cheats, its deposit is slashed, so a Sybil farm pays many times for one attack and gains nothing extra.
